Invalid JSON when parsing {"candidates":[{"candidate_id":"c1_generate-validate-repair_realistic","title":"Empirical evaluation of LLM generate–validate–repair pipelines with deterministic network verification under realistic topologies and failure injection","research_question":"Does composing an LLM with a deterministic network verifier in a generate–validate–repair loop reduce the rate of unsafe configuration deployments and what are the dominant failure modes under realistic topologies and injected faults?","hypotheses":["Integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM generate–validate–repair loop reduces the proportion of configurations that would be classified as unsafe by the verifier at deployment time by >50% compared to LLM-only generation under matched prompts and tasks.","When repairs are attempted, at least 70% of verifier-detected failures are resolved within three repair iterations; remaining failures are concentrated in tasks with ambiguous intents or topologies with richer policy interactions."],"proposed_design":"Preregistered three-arm, paired-task experiment using a public synthetic NetOps task set (10 realistic topologies × 20 intent tasks = 200 tasks). Arms: (A) LLM-only generation; (B) LLM + verifier (reject-only: if verifier fails, configuration is rejected); (C) LLM + verifier + iterative repair loop (up to 5 repair iterations). Use a deterministic network verifier (e.g., Batfish) to run static reachability, ACL, and BGP-policy checks and to produce failure diagnostics. Inject controlled faults per task (link failure, route flap, ACL conflict) in a repeatable manner. Use hosted-model API(s) from the allowed compute resources; freeze model identifiers, prompt templates, seeds, and maximum call budgets in preregistration. Archive all generated configs, verifier traces, and repair histories. Primary comparison is per-task paired verifier outcome between arms. Stopping rules: fixed budget of calls per task; retries only for infrastructure failures per preregistered policy.","expected_data":"For each of 200 tasks and three arms: generated configuration text, verifier pass/fail boolean, verifier failure diagnostics, number of repair iterations performed, per-iteration model outputs, end-to-end simulated reachability test results under injected faults, per-task latency and model-call counts. Aggregate counts: verifier-pass rates, repair-success rates, distribution of failure types, and per-task latency histograms.","primary_outcome":"Reduction in the proportion of tasks producing verifier-failing (unsafe) configurations accepted for deployment between LLM-only and the generate–validate–repair arm (primary metric: absolute and relative difference in unsafe-proportion).","analysis_outline":"Compute per-task paired comparisons of verifier-pass proportion between arms; use McNemar's test for paired binary outcomes and report 95% confidence intervals for difference in proportions. Estimate effect sizes (risk difference, relative risk). Model marginal effects using logistic regression controlling for topology complexity and task type. Report repair iteration survival curves and time-to-pass; perform failure-mode clustering on verifier diagnostics to identify systematic residual errors. Report exact p-values, CIs, and multiple-comparison adjustments where applicable.","novelty_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4401857375","doi:10.20944/preprints202604.1820.v1","https://openalex.org/W4392875514"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4396723768","doi:10.1002/nem.2313","https://openalex.org/W4401857375"],"risks":["Deterministic verifier may not model all operational dynamics (false negatives in verifier pass).","LLM repair loops may introduce oscillation or superficially-correct but semantically-incorrect changes (false sense of safety).","Engineering integration increases latency and operational complexity, raising deployment friction.","Dataset/topology design may under-represent corner cases leading to overoptimistic safety estimates."],"estimated_model_calls":1200},{"candidate_id":"c2_verifierbench_dataset_and_benchmark","title":"NetOps-VerifierBench: a public dataset and benchmark for verifier-grounded intent-to-configuration evaluation (ACL/BGP semantics)","research_question":"Can a publicly released dataset pairing operator intents with ground-truth configurations and deterministic-verifier labels enable reproducible evaluation of LLM-driven NetOps correctness and reveal current model failure modes relevant to operational safety?","hypotheses":["A verifier-grounded public benchmark will show that state-of-the-art hosted LLMs produce configurations that are inconsistent with deterministic verifier labels (verifier-inconsistency) on >40% of intent tasks under baseline prompts.","Providing verifier diagnostics and programmatic evaluation in the benchmark will reduce inter-run metric variance and enable reproducible comparison across models and prompts compared to ad-hoc textual correctness metrics."],"proposed_design":"Construct a curated public dataset of 5,000 intent→configuration examples covering ACL semantics (allow/deny intent variants) and BGP policy intents across multiple synthetic but realistic topologies. For each example include: natural-language intent, canonical config, deterministic verifier labels (reachability assertions, policy-preservation booleans), and diagnostic traces from a verifier (e.g., Batfish outputs). Generate canonical configs from publicly-available RFC examples, vendor docs, and synthesized variants; verify canonical configs with the verifier to produce ground-truth labels. Define benchmark tasks and evaluation harness (verifier-consistency, semantic-preservation, syntactic correctness). Release dataset, evaluation code, and baseline results for at least two hosted LLMs under frozen prompts and seeds. Follow privacy-preserving procedures and document synthesis provenance in metadata.","expected_data":"A machine-readable corpus: 5,000 labeled examples with intent text, canonical config, verifier boolean labels, diagnostic traces, topology metadata. Baseline model outputs and evaluation CSVs: verifier-pass rates, semantic-mismatch counts, syntactic-parse errors, and per-example diagnostics. Release includes README, license, and evaluation harness.","primary_outcome":"Public release of NetOps-VerifierBench plus baseline benchmark numbers (verifier-consistency rates for baseline models) and measurement of inter-run variance; demonstration that verifier-grounded labels produce lower evaluation variance and more operationally-relevant failure signals.","analysis_outline":"Report dataset statistics (task types, topology complexity distribution). Evaluate baseline LLMs on the benchmark under frozen prompts: compute verifier-consistency rate, semantic-preservation F1 if applicable, and syntactic error rate. Quantify evaluation variance across repeated runs and compare with textual-only metrics (e.g., BLEU/EM). Provide failure-mode taxonomies and representative examples. Validate reproducibility by re-running a subset of baseline evaluations and reporting reproducibility statistics.","novelty_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4392875514","https://openalex.org/W4411735779"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4392875514","https://openalex.org/W4396723768"],"risks":["Synthetic generation may bias examples and under-represent rare but critical operator scenarios.","Public release risks inadvertent exposure of sensitive configuration patterns—mitigate by synthesizing and anonymizing inputs.","Benchmark may be gamed by prompt-tuning to exploit superficial evaluation signals rather than genuine semantic correctness.","Deterministic verifier coverage limits validity for dynamic operational properties."],"estimated_model_calls":300},{"candidate_id":"c3_prompt-sensitivity_cross-model_vendor_cli","title":"Prompt-sensitivity and cross-model robustness for intent-to-configuration generation across vendor CLIs","research_question":"How sensitive are LLM intent-to-configuration translations to small prompt perturbations across different hosted LLMs and vendor-specific CLIs, and does prompt-coupling generalize across vendors?","hypotheses":["Minor prompt perturbations (synonym substitution, clause reordering, small format changes) cause >30% relative variance in verifier-consistency rates for at least one mainstream hosted LLM across vendor CLIs.","Prompt-template designs that explicitly couple intent, required invariants, and verifier-check instructions reduce cross-prompt variance in verifier-consistency compared to minimal prompts.",""],"proposed_design":"Cross-model, cross-prompt factorial experiment. Select two vendor CLIs (e.g., Cisco-like IOS, Juniper-like JUNOS syntactic families) and two hosted LLMs available in the environment. Define three base prompt templates (minimal intent, structured intent+constraints, and intent+example) and apply three systematic perturbations per template (synonym swap, clause reorder, minor punctuation change) producing 27 prompt variants. Run the prompts over 150 intent tasks (sampled across ACL and BGP intents). Evaluate generated configs with deterministic verifier for pass/fail and compute syntactic parse errors. Freeze models, prompt texts, and seeds in preregistration. Measure per-task variance attributable to prompt, model, and vendor using ANOVA.","expected_data":"For 150 tasks × 2 models × 2 vendor CLIs × 27 prompt variants: generated configurations, verifier pass/fail, syntactic parse outcome, per-run latency, and prompt variant metadata. Aggregates: per-prompt and per-model verifier-consistency distributions, variance components, and failure-mode examples highlighting vendor-specific brittleness.","primary_outcome":"Quantified prompt-induced variance in verifier-consistency (percentage of total variance attributable to prompt perturbations) and demonstration of whether structured prompt templates materially reduce variance across vendors and models.","analysis_outline":"Perform variance-component analysis (ANOVA) to partition variance attributable to prompt, model, vendor, and their interactions. Report effect sizes and confidence intervals. Use paired tests to compare structured prompts vs minimal prompts on verifier-pass rates. Provide qualitative analysis of representative prompt-sensitive failure cases and vendor-specific syntactic errors.","novelty_evidence_ids":["doi:10.2139/ssrn.6262638","https://openalex.org/W4406928793"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4401857375","doi:10.1002/nem.2313"],"risks":["Vendor CLI differences may confound prompt effects if parsers/normalizers are not properly modeled.","Prompt-engineering findings may be overfitted to the tested models and not generalize to future model versions.","High model-call counts may increase cost and latency for practical adoption."],"estimated_model_calls":1500},{"candidate_id":"c4_bounded_self_correction_tradeoffs","title":"Bounded self-correction: diminishing returns and operational trade-offs in iterative LLM repair loops for NetOps","research_question":"What are the effectiveness, latency, and cost trade-offs of bounding iterative LLM repair iterations in LLM+verifier pipelines for NetOps tasks, and at what iteration count do diminishing returns become operationally unjustified?","hypotheses":["A majority (>60%) of verifier-detected failures that are correctable by the LLM are resolved within three repair iterations; beyond three iterations the marginal verifier-consistency improvement is <5% while median latency increases linearly with iterations.","Setting a bounded repair policy at three iterations yields near-maximal safety improvement while reducing median per-task latency and model-call consumption relative to unbounded repair policies.",""],"proposed_design":"Using the same task bank as candidate c1 (200 tasks), run an LLM+verifier iterative repair pipeline with a maximum of 8 iterations per task. For each task record per-iteration outputs, verifier pass/fail, diagnostics, cumulative latency, and model-call counts. Compare bounded policies (max iterations = 1, 3, 5, 8) in an offline analysis to compute marginal gains and cost metrics. Predefine cost thresholds and stopping rules in preregistration (e.g., max total model calls per task). Archive raw artifacts for reproducibility.","expected_data":"Per-task per-iteration records: generated configuration, verifier boolean, diagnostic traces, cumulative latency, cumulative model calls. Aggregate per-policy metrics: verifier-pass rate, average iterations to pass, fraction unresolved, median latency, and model-call consumption distributions.","primary_outcome":"Identification of the iteration bound at which marginal verifier-consistency improvement falls below a pre-specified operational threshold (e.g., 5%) along with associated latency/model-call trade-offs to recommend a bounded repair policy.","analysis_outline":"Compute per-iteration marginal improvement in verifier-pass rate and plot cumulative improvement curves. Use change-point detection to identify inflection in marginal gains. Compare bounded policies using pairwise tests on verifier-pass rates and cost metrics (latency, model calls). Report trade-off frontiers and recommend operational bounds under different cost/latency constraints.","novelty_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4401857375","https://openalex.org/W4396723768","doi:10.20944/preprints202604.1820.v1"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4396723768","https://openalex.org/W4401857375"],"risks":["Iterative repairs can create oscillatory edits and may increase chance of semantic drift away from the original intent.","Adversarial or ambiguous intents may cause indefinite repair attempts if stopping bounds are not enforced.","Latency and cost increases may make bounded repair impractical for low-latency operational settings."],"estimated_model_calls":800}]} for TypeAdapter(CandidateSet); 2 validation errors for CandidateSet
